E001.text:
the boat was purchased from Joe Martinez III of San Antonio on December 1st 1994. Lester
Ducote went with me to San Antonio to close the sale and haul the boat
"Knock Down" to Austin. Bill Peace went with me to haul the boat to Port Aransas.
December 15th Arrangements were made with Dumas Marine for compounding, waxing,
bottom paint, teak work Etc. Island boat works handled the Electronic tune up
and the installation of trim tabs, Lowrance 350 GPS, washdown Etc. many short
runs up Lydia Ann waterway or toward Corpus Christi were made during this
shakedown period.

E004.text:
March 25th
Bill Hudspeth and Val England join Mike and me for a great snapper trip!
80 degrees of the bar to Big Red in 21 fathoms. We used cut squid (Big ones!) to
catch 2 large sow snapper - 24lbs and 20lbs and another 20 or so smaller ones.
Beautiful weather NO seas light north wind. cruising speed out and back was 25 knots.
E004.note: Big Red an oil platform painted in red primer paint.

E-9b5808e48b.text: May 20th: Bill Hudspeth, Mike Fleming & I fish a rig, hooked at (N27°53.152, W96°44.925). Mile caught a big king - weight unknown, but he  was 55 inches long, one bite - a 24 inch girth. 2 other less lucky than Mike caught two atlantic sharpnose that made his trip - wind ENE 15kt. Rough but lots of sunshine good time!

E-8dd394a776.text: Memorial Day Weekend - Wind still Howling - got out Saturday with Frank Niendorf, sons David and Will and of course Mike Fleming went to back to above noted rig - Caught one shark - missed two others - seas got to 6-8' so we came in
E-8dd394a776.note: I was pissed off because Neindorf missed a gaff on my white tip shark. The next day I wrote a note on the steering wheel that read "no one allowed on this boat that doesn't know how to gaff"

E-77f97f0ab3.text: June 9th: too rough for us to take Seahawk out so Mike and I go out on the Wharf Cat - Rough seas - Mike wins pot of $51! with a 12lb King Maybe sometime this summer the wind will stop!
E-77f97f0ab3.note: Wind hardly ever stopped that summer, says the captain.

E-f80d412081.text: June 30th   Bill Hudspeth, Mike & I fish Scorpion Rig - we catch two king and three shark, in one hour.
E-f80d412081.note: Scoprion Rig had two big cranes coming off the sides, looked like one was its tail and one was its head.

E-aabe25e19a.text: July 12th -  1st day of the Deep Sea Roundup Tournament - Gary Einkhoff, Me, Lester, Alex & Michael head out in 6 foot seas to just short of Big Red. Squalls convince us to head N-NW to Mighty Whitey Rig. Windy. We catch a 33 pounder (Lester), a 22 pounder (Alex) and a 22 pounder (Mike). Alex & Mike were in first and second place at end of Day one.
E-aabe25e19a.note: Dad says this was a rough day, six foot seas! Mighty Whitey Rig was an inshore rig painted entirely white.

E-6275f088f2.text: July 26th   We head out on 78° to Big Red - beautiful day! Running 3,000 RPM all day. Not much luck at Big Red or Val's Rig. Then we go to Satellite Rig. Alex catches a 22 pound snapper that wins the junior and senior division of the tournament for Snapper. We also catch 20 or so other Snapper 2 pounds to 6 pounds. We trolled back in with no takers except amberjack. We caught and released several short of legal limit.

E-15669bb080.text:
July 7th  Outboard tournament - Mike, Einlauf & me
beautiful seas - all the way to Baker Reef - No luck!  10 gallons per hour.
E-15669bb080.note: They split up the tournament by engine spec, outboard tournament was our time to shine. Baker Reef was one of the coral reefs offshore. Baker, South Baker, Southern, and Hospital were all about 40 miles out. They catch marlin, sailfish, and wahoo out there.

E-243dafc8f0.text: July 8th Opt.  Went north to the Way Ups then East to Satellite. 10 snappers, lots of chicken dolphin in weed lines. Other than that no luck trolling - beautiful calm day  10 gallons per hour.
E-243dafc8f0.note: The Way Ups were a cluster of rigs about 35 miles North of the jetty's that were in shallow water.

E-06e80bdd06.text:
July 15th  Took Mike hornsby and friend, Jenny, to Lone Pipe.
Caught 6 Kings in about 20 minutes - came home in
beautiful weather - depth record out, also fuel pump
between the auxilary and the main fuel line must have a constriction.
Next week don't buy bait - we have 20 pounds of squid and ribbon fish in the freezer.
E-06e80bdd06.note: Lone Pipe was just a big ol' standpipe gas well sticking out of the water. Covered in barnacles, which attract fish.

E-d779898898.text:
July 29th  Guests were Dr Scott Holt and Dr Steve ___ from the
University of Texas Marine Science Center. We left at 6:30 am
- Calm seas - Went to Scorpion only one king, then to Val's Rig
when the current was running so swiftly to the NORTH that we could not tie on.
E-d779898898.note: They ended up naming Val's Rig after Val England where she caught those snapper there in one of the earlier trips.

E-be19a07009.text:
We proceeded off shore about 1/2 mile where we found a great sargassom weed line. 
We stopped and chummed up six dolphin (3 to 4 lbs) and a 15 lb Wahoo. Dr. Holt's first Wahoo and Dr Steve's first Dolphin. We Ended the day at Big Red, catching and 27 Vermillion and red Snapper - Seas roughed up way home - N. wind 3-4 ft - Tropical Depression heading our way. Wahoo and Dolphin caught on Ballyhoo under an Octopus skirt
E-be19a07009.note: Vermillion are a type of snapper bright red as the name implies even brighter than red snapper, with some yellow along the gill plates. More importantly there wasn't a limit on them at the time, according to the Captain.

E-61f45f40e7.text: 8/1/98 - Charles,and Judy Durban; after 2 days of waiting out Tropical Storm Gabriel, we make it out on a heading 85° (to the East)to 95 feet of water - lots of shrimp boats - caught 6 Kings real fast, no size though - all 12-20 lbs. Squally day - 4' to 5' seas, some rain. Again we used Ballyhoo under seven strang octopus yellow and green one great bait!

E-8f1abd29f1.text:
8/15  Chris Carothers, Mike Fleming, Nicole Beasley & me -
Beautiful day! We leave at 7:00 - hit weed line at 80 degrees in about 19  fathoms. Caught two nice dolphins.  10 -12 pounds. Weed line was patchy, and only about 300 yds, long.
Seas running from the southeast to the north west. Then we go to Val's Rig past Big Red where we caught a limit of Kings (12). A big shark (unseen but big by bight angle) Cut three of our kings off right behind the gills! - Fast action on Kings, 2 on at at once a few times! Also caught 8 or so snapper one at 6 lbs the largest.

I was the only witness. The shark was about as big as a suburban. It had at least 25 stripes. It probably was 325 pounds.
E-8f1abd29f1.note: That bottom note is from me, Mike. I remember seeing that big sucker come up under the boat as we were tied off on the rig! Everyone must have been sick of me because no one wanted to come up and look at it. Too bad they missed out!

E-5a8d69156d.text:
8/20 - Dr. Scott Holt & Dr. Joan Holt on board with Mike and me. We
ended up gooing north to the Way Ups. No kings taken
no much sign of life until we tied on to a Way Up and cauught a limit of nice snapper, release a 10 pound king. beautiful day.
